title: SME Knowledge Review
markdown:
Knowledge that reaches a specialist passes through a subject-matter-expert (SME) review gate. The queue and its decisions live in `openexecutive.knowledge.review_store.ReviewStore`, which shares the `./episodic_memory.db` SQLite database with episodic memory.

### Shipped knowledge is trusted on arrival

The ~81 Markdown files under `knowledge/builtin/` are curated upstream and ship with the product. They register as **trusted defaults** — `approved`, with a NULL `reviewed_at` — so a new instance starts with an **empty** review queue and the Executive can draw on that material immediately. The same applies to manifest-listed external (OER) sources.

Provenance is an explicit `trusted_default` column, fed by a committed manifest — it is never inferred. That matters more than it looks: a document a user creates through the knowledge UI is *also* `pending` with a NULL `reviewed_at`, **and** it is written into the same `knowledge/builtin/` tree the shipped docs live in. So neither the status shape nor the presence of a file on disk can tell the two apart. `sync_builtin_registrations` walks `SHIPPED_BUILTIN_FILES` rather than the directory, and `register()` — the path user uploads take — never sets the flag.

Identity is namespaced to match. Failure case studies ship under `knowledge/builtin/failures/<domain>/` and register as `failure:<domain>:<file>`, **not** `builtin:<domain>:<file>`. That second namespace is the one `POST /knowledge/builtin` writes into, and because no file sits at `knowledge/builtin/<domain>/<file>` for a failure doc, that route's "file already exists" guard could not fire — an upload of the same name landed on the shipped row and inherited its trust. A one-shot migration re-keys existing rows, carrying the reviewer's status, notes and annotations across.

Read together with `reviewed_at`:

| State | `reviewed_at` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `approved` + `trusted_default` | *NULL* | **Trusted default** — shipped with the product, nobody here has vetted it |
| `approved` | set | An SME signed off, and can promote the item in priority |
| `pending` | — | Deliberately queued for curation |
| `rejected` | set | An SME rejected it |
| `needs_revision` | — | Was decided on; the content has since been edited |

An install that predates this registers its shipped docs as `pending`. `ReviewStore.backfill_trusted_defaults()` promotes them once, guarded by a marker row in `review_meta`. It runs *after* the registration syncs, because it only touches rows they have flagged as shipped — a user's own upload awaiting review is never approved on their behalf.

Its rule is that **no shipped doc loses retrievability on upgrade**: the sole exclusion is an explicit SME decision (which always stamps `reviewed_at`). Reviewer notes and annotations do not hold a row back — annotations are injected into specialist context by domain regardless of item status, so withholding an annotated doc would hand the Executive a correction to a document it can no longer see.

### Effect on retrieval

An item is **withheld** when it is `pending` *or* `rejected`. Withheld items are filtered out of every retrieval — `retrieve` for the built-in and external collections, and `retrieve_failures` for the failure case studies, which share the same review registrations but live in their own Chroma collection.

Because shipped content defaults to approved, `pending` genuinely means *a human deliberately queued this*, which is what makes withholding it safe. `needs_revision` is deliberately **not** withheld: an item lands there on any content edit, so withholding it would make editing a file in the knowledge UI silently drop it from retrieval.

### Curation is opt-in, one domain at a time

`POST /review/curate` with `{"domain": "finance", "action": "start"}` moves that domain's untouched trusted defaults into the queue; `"stop"` puts them back. Neither direction disturbs an item an SME actually decided on.

`domain` is required. There is no "curate everything" selector, because curating withholds content — no single call should be able to take the whole knowledge base away from the Executive. The UI names the exact count before it starts.

`POST /review/bulk-approve` clears the queue again, selecting by `domain`, an explicit `item_ids` list (over 500 is rejected rather than silently truncated), or `all_pending: true`. A call carrying no selector is rejected, and so is an empty `domain` — the store reads a falsy domain as "no filter", so accepting one would quietly turn a scoped approve into a blanket one. Both endpoints write audit events (`review_bulk_approve`, `review_curate`).

### SME annotations

Alongside a status, an SME can attach **annotations** — free-text corrections stored in `review_annotations` and injected into retrieved context for the item's domain. They let an expert correct or localize shipped material without editing the underlying file.
